title_en: Place a single image before the text
content_en: If the request contains a single image, place the image before the text prompt in the request.
applies_when_en: One source image and a text instruction for it go into the call, or several references that the prompt text refers to by number (Image 1, the first image).
not_applies_when_en: A call without images; Imagen customization, where references are addressed by referenceId (see the rule on Imagen customization references).
caveats_en: The advice comes from the best practices for image understanding models; the multi-image REST request there interleaves image and text parts (models: other).
For image generation and editing the advice is not stated: official generation and editing samples use different part orders and prescribe none; contents is an ordered list (models: unspecified).
In the multi-image REST request, image and text parts are interleaved in order: image 1, text 1, image 2, text 2, image 3; this is an inference (models: unspecified).

The recipes notebook does not treat part order as meaningful: images usually precede the text, but the style-transfer recipe puts the text first; only the try-on prompt relies on order ("first image", "second image"); this is an inference (models: nb25).

title_en: Generate illustrations from live structured data
content_en: Build the prompt from live data: on a schedule, an app reads structured data (for example, calendar events and the weather), then prompts the model to generate a personalized illustration that reflects the data. Automating creative workflows, such as personalized marketing assets at scale, is a suggested application.
applies_when_en: The prompt is assembled automatically from structured data (a calendar, the weather, a product card) and the image carries practical information.
caveats_en: The suggested application of automating creative workflows comes from a hackathon for Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (models: nb25).
The app uses Gemini 3.6 Flash alongside the image model (models: other).
The app description names Nano Banana without a version (models: unspecified).

The app was built by a creative technologist with Gemini 3.6 Flash and Nano Banana; its code is open-sourced (github.com/google-gemini/glanceboard) so users can ask Google Antigravity to build one (models: unspecified).
The resulting illustration encodes practical information (what to wear, what to pack) visually for a low-power e-ink screen; this is an inference (models: unspecified).
